_doc: Frozen figure proportion (director, 2026-10-08: proportion C 'B/W-like', 56 px, pitch 55; chosen from docs/audits/proportion_samples/). render_character.py applies it by default. Pose bones only: uniform bone scales (no bone added or renamed, so the frozen skeleton in rig_contract.json and Mixamo clips still apply), then the deformed figure is refitted to the reference height (camera_rig.json reference_height_m) with its feet on the ground. Clips must not key bone scale (strip scale curves on import) or they would undo it. The stance block is the rest-pose stance only: the frozen A-pose reads as a hunch at 55 degrees, so the upper arms and forearms are aimed down; clips supply their own rotations.

bw.label: C B/W-LIKE
bw.bone_scale_doc: Lead QC 2026-10-09: arms 0.85 like the thighs, so the hands hang at mid-thigh (B/W trainer proportion) instead of at the knee. A child inherits its parent's scale, so the hands are 1.53 = 1.3 / 0.85 to stay 1.3x the realistic hand; the forearm follows the upper arm.
bw.recentre_doc: Lead QC 2026-10-09: scaling the head 1.8x about its joint pushed the face forward of the shoulders with no neck. The head's horizontal offset from the neck joint is shrunk back to its natural (unscaled) size, keep_offset 1/1.8, and lifted 1.5 cm to show a neck (pose-bone translation only). Centring it fully on the spine put the head behind the neck and tore the neck skin (side-on render, 2026-10-09).

pose.doc: rest stance: world directions with the body facing -Y and left = +X; upper arms 12 degrees off vertical, forearms 6, legs nearly vertical
pose.stance_doc: Lead QC 2026-10-09: the rest pose stood 0.37 m wide, so in the E and W facings the far foot (planted, measured z equal) drew about 16 px higher at 55 degrees and read as lifted. Thighs and shins are aimed nearly straight down to bring the feet under the hips.
